headline: Last session: Sensex fell 289 points on inflation concerns, but markets extended gains for a third straight week.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 17 November.

why: Inflation concerns weighed on equity markets, leading Sensex to fall 289 points in the last session.
Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) buying helped Indian markets gain for a third consecutive week.
Lower crude oil prices and strong foreign inflows provided early support to benchmark indices.
Markets are evaluating upcoming domestic WPI inflation data and global economic cues.
whatHappening: Max Estates received HARERA approval for a ₹4,000 crore luxury housing project in Gurugram.
RBI announced a review of the ₹3 lakh income threshold for microfinance borrowers.
Air purifier sales experienced a surge in NCR as air quality index deteriorated sharply.
Multiple stocks including ENS Enterprises and Shankesh Jewellers face IPO lock-in expiry between Nov 16-20.
summary: In the last trading session, the Sensex dropped 289 points as inflation concerns dented market sentiment. Despite daily pressure, Indian benchmarks managed to secure gains for the third consecutive week thanks to continued FII buying. Markets are closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Tuesday, 17 November.
